description: This file implements ARMv7 MMU support for Zephyr OS, including page table setup, memory mapping/unmapping, and address translation functions.

methods.name: invalidate_tlb_all
methods.description: Invalidates the entire TLB to ensure consistency after page table changes.

methods.name: arm_mmu_assign_l2_table
methods.description: Allocates and returns a free level 2 page table, updating internal tracking.

methods.name: arm_mmu_release_l2_table
methods.description: Releases a level 2 page table, marking it as available for reuse.

methods.name: arm_mmu_inc_l2_table_entries
methods.description: Increments the count of used entries in a level 2 page table.

methods.name: arm_mmu_dec_l2_table_entries
methods.description: Decrements the count of used entries in a level 2 page table, releasing it if count reaches zero.

methods.name: arm_mmu_convert_attr_flags
methods.description: Converts system memory attribute flags into MMU-specific permission and attribute bits.

methods.name: arm_mmu_l1_map_section
methods.description: Maps a 1MB section in the level 1 page table with specified attributes.

methods.name: arm_mmu_remap_l1_section_to_l2_table
methods.description: Converts a level 1 section mapping into a full level 2 page table for fine-grained control.

methods.name: arm_mmu_l2_map_page
methods.description: Maps a 4KB page in a level 2 page table with specified attributes.

methods.name: arm_mmu_l2_unmap_page
methods.description: Unmaps a 4KB page by clearing its level 2 page table entry.

methods.name: z_arm_mmu_init
methods.description: Initializes the MMU at boot time, setting up page tables and memory regions.

methods.name: __arch_mem_map
methods.description: Maps a memory region at runtime with specified attributes and permissions.

methods.name: arch_mem_map
methods.description: Wrapper around __arch_mem_map, triggers panic on failure.

methods.name: __arch_mem_unmap
methods.description: Unmaps a memory region at runtime.

methods.name: arch_page_phys_get
methods.description: Resolves the physical address for a given virtual address.
